concepts.label: Maximum TTL setting
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the bucket- and collection-level maxTTL ceiling this page documents in depth

relations.subject: data:expiration
relations.evidence: You can change the document's expiration by setting its expiration value during a mutation.

relations.subject: n1ql:update
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - a mutation that does not explicitly set expiration silently clears any existing expiration to 0, unless a non-zero maxTTL is in force
relations.evidence: By default, if you mutate a document without setting its expiration, Couchbase Server automatically sets the value to 0.

relations.subject: n1ql:update
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the preserve_expiry request-level parameter is the documented workaround for the auto-clear behavior above
relations.evidence: You can prevent Couchbase Server from clearing the expiration value by using the [preserve\_expiry](../n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md#preserve%5Fexpiry) request-level parameter.

relations.subject: data:max-ttl-setting
relations.evidence: You cannot explicitly set a document's expiration to be longer than the `maxTTL` setting. If you try to set the expiration to a value larger than the collection or bucket's `maxTTL` setting, Couchbase Server uses the `maxTTL` value instead.

relations.subject: server:collection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - a collection-level maxTTL of 0 falls back to the bucket's own maxTTL setting; genuinely not stated on THIS page, which only ever discusses collection-or-bucket maxTTL jointly
relations.evidence: The `maxTTL` for the collection is `0`, which means documents use the `maxTTL` setting from the bucket.
relations.evidence_provenance: cross-page: manage-expiration.md states maxTTL applies jointly to 'the collection or bucket' but never states which one wins when both are set; the fallback direction (collection maxTTL of 0 defers to the bucket's) is stated only on the sibling manage-scopes-and-collections.md page in this same batch.

notable_absence.finding: The page opens with 'You can have documents in your Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition automatically expire after a period of time' - implying automatic (maxTTL-driven) expiration is an Enterprise-only capability. But the rest of the page never repeats or qualifies this restriction, and the per-document expiration examples (SQL++ INSERT/UPDATE, SDK insert) are not marked Enterprise-only elsewhere in the corpus. This reads as either an overclaim in the introduction or an underspecified one everywhere else on the page - flagged rather than resolved, since no other sentence on this page confirms or narrows the edition scope.
